channel.title: Am I affected? changelog
channel.description: Every check added to Am I affected?, newest first.

item.title: macOS and Firefox are checked
item.description: macOS is flagged when it lacks the fix for CVE-2026-86950, a CoreGraphics bug Apple says was exploited in targeted attacks (Tahoe 26.7.1, Sequoia 15.8.1), or when it is Sonoma 14 or older, which no longer get fixes. Firefox is flagged before 159.0.1, ESR 153.6 or ESR 115.44; its version is read from disk, so Firefox isn't started. Behind the scenes, the vendors' own zero-day notes (Chrome, Apple, Mozilla) now reach our queue the day they are published.

item.title: Chrome before 157.0.8103.50 is flagged
item.description: Google fixed CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free in Chrome's XML code that is being exploited, on 9 Nov in 157.0.8103.50. Older Chrome and Chromium, and the Puppeteer and Playwright browsers older than that, are now flagged. Update and relaunch the browser.

item.title: A second review of the tool's own code
item.description: A review against its own design notes found and fixed: --update now refuses an older signed script served beside newer signed data (advisories.json names the script's SHA-256); scanning a repo with a symlink to /dev/zero no longer reads forever; a vendor condition the tool can't judge can't produce a notice through negation; more kernel builds (64k, debug) are left to you by --fix; a torn audit-log line or a cut-off download no longer crashes the tool; when CISA's exploited list can't be loaded it says so; watch mode reports a second affected install of the same thing.

item.title: --fix leaves every kernel to you
item.description: Kernel updates found through the vendor's notices are no longer offered by --fix: like the hand-picked kernel checks, they need a reboot, so the fix plan lists them for you to do. The GitHub Action now makes no network calls at all, as its description says.

item.title: Debian packages against Debian's own notices
item.description: Debian 11, 12 and 13 now get the same check of every installed package, against the security tracker's notices. Debian rates no severity, so a package is AFFECTED only when one of its CVEs is on CISA's exploited list; the rest are REVIEW and --fix offers them. A package a hand-picked check already flags now shows as one row, not two. Checked on Debian 12.0: everything apt would upgrade from the security archive, glibc first for CVE-2023-4911.

item.title: Every installed package, against the vendor's notices
item.description: On Ubuntu, RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky and Oracle Linux the tool now lists every installed package and matches it against the vendor's own security notices (USN, RHSA, ALSA, ELSA), downloaded to the server and matched there. Anything on CISA's exploited list comes first. --fix offers these updates too. Checked against apt and dnf's own security lists on six distro images.

item.title: --fix runs only from signed code
item.description: --fix now runs only from the installed copy (--install), and first checks that its files still match their signatures. If anything was edited after install, it changes nothing and says to run --update. A scheduled job also checks every 6 hours that the files on the site verify.

item.title: Homebrew packages that are behind
item.description: nginx, httpd, MariaDB, MongoDB and Brotli installed with Homebrew (on a Mac or Linuxbrew) are now checked against the upstream fixes, like vendor packages on Linux. --fix offers brew upgrade for them, and watch mode says when the fix is available.

item.title: Install once, update only from signed releases
item.description: --install keeps a copy in /opt/amiaffected with our release key pinned. --update takes a new release only when secinspect.py and advisories.json are both signed by that key and the data isn't older than what's installed; otherwise nothing changes and it says why. Every install, update and refusal goes into the audit log. The signing key stays offline.

item.title: Watch mode tells you when a fix is ready
item.description: When the fixed build of an affected package shows up in your server's package sources, from the distro or a vendor repository, watch mode sends one PATCH line saying so, ready for --fix. It never installs anything from cron.

item.title: Apply fixes with your approval
item.description: --fix offers the update for each affected package through apt, dnf or Homebrew, from your distro or a vendor repository you added, and runs it only when you type yes. It checks again afterwards and writes every step to a local audit log that shows if a line was changed (--verify-log).

item.title: Chromium before 157.0.8103.38
item.description: Chrome's 3 November release fixes 196 bugs, 33 of them critical, several of which run code outside the sandbox. Playwright 1.65.0 already ships a fixed build; Puppeteer 25.16.0 doesn't yet, so the advice is still to run it on your installed Chrome.

item.title: The CVE queue runs every 6 hours
item.description: New CVEs are picked up four times a day instead of once, and a feed that reorders itself no longer opens a second issue for the same release.

item.title: Agent watchlist
item.description: One page listing the skills, MCP servers and extensions named in public as malicious or unsafe, each with its source, how the tool finds it and what to do. Generated from the same data the tool reads, at amiaffected.now/watchlist.

item.title: WordPress CVE-2026-119977 is now exploited
item.description: CISA added the core upgrade race condition to its exploited list, with a 6 November deadline for US federal agencies. The check already flagged it; the label now says it is being exploited.

item.title: Watch mode stays quiet when an update doesn't fix anything
item.description: A kernel or package update that leaves the same bug open is no longer reported as one new and one fixed finding. Found by running watch mode on our own server.

item.title: Kernel advice no longer mentions AlmaLinux on Ubuntu
item.description: A note meant for RHEL-family servers was shown on every distro.

item.title: Watch mode for servers
item.description: Run it daily from cron with --watch and hear only about new and fixed findings, by webhook (Slack, Teams, Discord) or through your own sendmail. A quiet day sends nothing.

item.title: GitHub Action
item.description: uses: abhay-avagama/security-inspector@v1 checks a repository on every push: pinned packages, MCP configs, agent skills and .env files, never the runner itself.

item.title: Skill change tracking
item.description: --skills-baseline FILE records a fingerprint of every installed agent skill and lists new skills and changed files on the next run.

item.title: Agent skill and hook audit
item.description: Every installed skill is checked for hidden instructions, invisible characters, curl | sh installs, downloaded programs, credential reads, persistence and the authors Snyk's ToxicSkills research confirmed malicious. Plugin hooks are listed with the events that run them.

item.title: Cursor marketplace Claude Code extension backdoor
item.description: Flags any trace of the tampered 2.1.312 / 2.1.313 builds from 29 October: the svc-telemetry SSH key, its persistence files, launch agent and cron entry.

item.title: Ubuntu's -proposed kernels for CVE-2026-98432
item.description: A booted -proposed kernel now counts as fixed, and the fix plan gives Ubuntu's own steps to install it.

item.title: AI agent setup audit
item.description: Unpinned MCP servers, coding agents allowed to run any command, SSH keys without a passphrase and .env files in folders agents work in. Reported as review, never as affected.

item.title: PostgreSQL, psqlODBC and pgAdmin 4
item.description: The August server and client release (fixed in 18.6 / 17.11 / 16.15 / 15.19 / 14.24), the psqlODBC batch fixed in 18.00.0006, and pgAdmin 4, whose fixes aren't released yet.

item.title: python-jose, @fastify/http-proxy, FreeRDP, WordPress plugins, Control Web Panel
item.description: Five fits from the week's critical CVEs, plus npm lockfile support (package-lock, pnpm, yarn, bun).

item.title: Chromium before 156.0.8078.73
item.description: The four critical bugs fixed on 27 October. The latest Playwright and Puppeteer still ship older builds, so the advice is to run them on your installed Chrome with the sandbox on.

item.title: A daily queue of new CVEs
item.description: Every morning a job opens an issue for each newly exploited or newly published CVE the tool doesn't cover yet, so nothing waits for us to notice it.

item.title: macOS Chrome GPU sandbox escape
item.description: CVE-2026-106378, fixed in 155.0.8059.39, flagged on Macs only.

item.title: Exploited Chrome bugs, stale Puppeteer and Playwright browsers, archived MCP servers
item.description: Installed Chrome, the Chromium copies Puppeteer and Playwright cache and never update, and MCP configs still running the archived Puppeteer server. Also SECURITY.md and private vulnerability reporting.

item.title: Linux servers
item.description: On Ubuntu, Debian and RHEL-family servers: the running kernel, nginx, Apache, MariaDB, MongoDB, WordPress and more, judged against each distro's own fixed packages.

item.title: amiaffected.now and the one-liner
item.description: curl -fsSL https://amiaffected.now/run | sh, readable before you run it.

item.title: Stale-data warning
item.description: Each run checks the public cve.now feed and warns when newer CVEs exist for what it tracks. Nothing about your machine is sent.

item.title: First release
item.description: The October 2026 PHP, Node.js, BIND, LiteLLM, GitLab and eMudhra issues, Docker image scanning and a fix plan with the exact commands.
